title: The River It Never Saw
concept: A Caltech and MIT preprint (arXiv 2610.22549, October 15th) called CFC26 is a benchmark for AI that counts salmon in sonar video, with 11 sites on 9 river systems, four in Alaska (three on the Kenai and one on the Nushagak). Held out of training, the Kenai banks still miss by under 0.07 and 0.03 with a direction score near zero and the Nushagak by about 0.035, the Kenai channel doubles from 0.14 to 0.29 and California's Mad River goes from about a third to 0.80. The preprint reports no agency use. The agency's sonar is drawn faceless and fully lit. The model is Wedge, a faced sonar fan labelled THE MODEL that first appears at the question, and a pale gold center line is the throughline: bare, ruled with tallies, a needle, half dashed into the dark, an open hook. A dashed unlit fan with a question mark is planted in the first frame and is the question the film pays at the end with an honest blank.

divergence_note: The last films were a bright civic hall of sage and honey with a ballot box (10-26), a rain boardwalk of signs (10-25), a navy orbit (10-24), a paper building in snow (10-23) and a dark tundra bob (10-22). This film is a near-black submerged sonar world lit by one mint fan, with amber fish echoes, a gold line and violet dashes. There is no hall, no desk of sliding sheets, no podium, no ballot, no boardwalk, no calendar and no scale. Its hero is a wedge-shaped instrument with a face, a new silhouette, and its world is the instrument's own screen plus a river bank near plane.

treatment.winner: dramatist structure (The Dark Half of the Fan) grafted with comedian hero face and Contrarian-free counting gags, explainer centre-line cutaway, enthusiast moose button
treatment.reasoning: Scored on scroll-stop, arc, retention, fairness, feasibility, freshness. The Dramatist's black right third of the fan present from frame one makes the withheld number a picture, not a promise; its Test (The Small Creek) draws the strongest fair case at full strength. Grafts: Comedian's faced Wedge with tally wheels and the digit overflow gag (hero needs a face for Emotion); Explainer's line-crossing cutaway because the preprint states humans count crossings of a centre line (verified); Enthusiast's near-zero compass needle high point and unimpressed moose. REJECTED: Comedian's Contrarian wrong-way blob (reads as the model miscounting); Explainer/Enthusiast derived 'ten fish a second' (full-day coverage unverified); Enthusiast 'right neighborhood' line (implies beats-humans).
treatment.revision_2026-10-28: After Gates 0B and 0D: the agency's counts are drawn on a FACELESS fully lit bank sonar (tally wheels, no eyes, no black sector); the faced Wedge is labelled THE MODEL and first appears at the question (S6); the expert hand count has a person with a clicker and no machine boxes (S4); the moose is on the lit near bank; the violet and coral roles are exclusive; VO 'didn't lean high or low' became 'the lean stayed near zero' per c14.
treatment.revision_2026-10-28b: Story corrected after the fact-check read Table 7's held-out column: Alaska sites mostly held up, the Kenai channel doubled, California's Mad River broke, and the open question is use in the field. The model's dark third now closes as held-out gauges stop low, the question boxes sit over the dashed unlit fan, the moose is cut.

angle.thesis: Hold a river out of training and the preprint's AI still counted Alaska's big rivers closely (Kenai banks under 7 and 3 percent, Nushagak about 3.5 percent) while a small California river broke (0.33 to 0.80), so what the preprint leaves open is not the held-out test but use in the field.
supporting_facts: c15 Kenai bank misses under 0.07 and 0.03 across all training conditions including held out (0.069, 0.025), direction near zero
c23 Kenai-Channel doubled when held out, 0.143 to 0.286
c18 Mad River 0.33 to 0.80 held out, a California river whose fish the preprint calls small and sparse
c19 built for deployment, no agency use reported
angle.counterpoint_honored: The Kenai channel site doubled when held out, three California rivers broke, the benchmark is one team's offline preprint, and the informal 10 percent human figure is a different ruler. Alaska's strong held-out numbers are a result on recorded video, not use in the field.
angle.falsifiable: False if the held-out Alaska values were as large as the California ones, or if the preprint reported an agency using it.
runner_ups: upside-only: home-water win (boosterish, hides the held-out test)
volume-hook only: 855,936 in a day (kept as the cold open, not the thesis)
angle.cross_challenge: All three analysts converged. Challenges applied: never say beats humans (0.07/0.03 vs informal 10 percent are different measures); Mad River always tagged California and small-count; no cause for any error; no ADF&G AI use; Nushagak -0.65 cut.
angle.correction_2026-10-28: An earlier draft said the preprint reports no held-out Alaska number. Table 7 (OOD column) does report one for every Alaska site, and they are low except the Kenai channel. The film was rebuilt on the verified table.
